core_claim: For open-ended research-agent tasks, structured disagreement among diverse critics is a better selection signal than a single scalar judge score.
challenged_premise: One judge can approximate research quality well enough to guide open-ended proposal selection.
first_principles_basis: Novel research lacks ground truth. Robustness is better approximated by independent attempts to find fatal flaws under different assumptions.
cross_domain_connections: diffusion denoising as iterative removal of error modes
measurable_prediction: Ideas selected by disagreement-pattern routing will have fewer shared fatal flaws in a held-out critic pass than ideas selected by a single judge score.

experiment_design.setup: Generate 12 candidate research ideas from the same seed. Review each with three critic profiles: skeptical empiricist, rigorous theoretician, pragmatic engineer. Select top ideas using either single score or disagreement-pattern routing. Run a held-out critic panel on selected ideas.
experiment_design.success_criterion: Disagreement-selected ideas produce fewer unanimous fatal-flaw findings and more evidence-grounded revision actions.
experiment_design.weakest_link: Critic independence may be weaker than assumed if all critics share the same base model.
experiment_design.critic_diversity_plan: Use different prompt priors, different scoring rubrics, and require each critic to cite a distinct failure mode or evidence gap.

risk_factors: critic prompts may create superficial diversity only
single judge may already internalize multiple criteria
held-out critic may share the same blind spots
